live_sim.use_for: set_breakage_thresholds() in the PhysX path (WP5 training)

bricksim_settings.warning: THE SAME PHYSICAL JOINT NEEDS DIFFERENT KNOB VALUES IN THE TWO PATHS: 18.832 N in static_solve and 120 N in the live sim both produce ~11.3 N/stud on a 2x4. Using one value in both paths misrepresents the joint by about 6.4x. Anything reading this file must pick the path it is running in.

measurement.method: pure axial pull-off, bisected on clutch utilisation crossing 1.0, via the patched static_solve

limitations: the fitted preloaded_force is calibrated against the STATIC solver only; the dynamic path releases at roughly 0.4x that prediction and its calibration is still provisional (see 'dynamic')
literature-calibrated, not derived: the [MechanicsSnapFit] closed-form relations were not applied and no mechanical phase was identified (§WP2 steps 1-2 not done, fallback taken)
asymmetry is IMPOSED by setting required_force (insertion) below the clutch capacity (extraction); BrickSim's static model does not produce insertion/extraction asymmetry emergently
1xN bricks do not share the 2xN per-stud capacity and are fitted separately; the plan library must not assume one number
calibrated against the static solver only; the in-sim PhysX path is assumed to share BreakageThresholds but is unverified

dynamic.why: WP5 trains in the live PhysX path. The static fit predicted 90.4 N release on a 2x4 where the dynamic path gives ~36.8 N, so the static preload would hand the policy a joint about 2.4x too weak.
dynamic.method: one Kit process per measurement (scripts/02_dynamic_sweep.sh); pure axial ramp at 0.1 N per physics step, release detected from get_disassembled_connections filtered to the article

total_force_ceiling.finding: release force saturates near 88-90 N per connection REGARDLESS of mated stud count, so per-stud capacity falls as bricks get larger instead of staying constant
total_force_ceiling.consequence: the report's §2.3 target of 8-15 N per stud CANNOT be met across the brick library at one setting: at preload 120 a 2x4 sits at 11.2 N/stud (in envelope) while a 2x6 sits at 7.4 N/stud (below the 8 N floor). Smaller bricks are correspondingly over-strength.
total_force_ceiling.sensitivity_warning: in the saturated region the knob barely works -- raising preload from 70 to 120 (+71%) buys 4.8% more release force, so the calibration is stiff against further tuning
